header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Time: 09:00 AM PT - 10:15 AM PT
Duration: 75 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom) + offices (SF / Dublin / Bangalore)
Attendees: Avery Chen (CEO); Maya Patel (CTO); Jon Rivera (CFO); Leah Gomez (Head of Product); Chris Nolan (Head of Sales); Samir Das (VP Engineering); Priya Singh (Head of People); plus ~120 employees via livestream
Recording link: https://redwood.zoom/rec/2026-08-25-allhands (internal)
summary: Leadership gave updates on Q3 goals and product launches: Redwood Dedicated scaling, Private deployment pilots, and Redwood Optimize early adopters. Finance shared updated ARR run rate and burn runway improvements. Engineering summarized kernel optimizations and KV cache improvements. Product announced roadmap milestones and a small reprioritization to accelerate private deployment features. Q&A covered pricing, region availability, SOC2 timeline, and hiring plans. Next steps captured for product deck, benchmarks, and security artifacts.
topics: Product roadmap updates: Dedicated, Private, Optimize
Engineering improvements: kernel selection, batching, caching
Security & compliance: SOC2/ISO and audit timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Avery (CEO): Hey everyone good morning, uh welcome to the August all hands. Thanks for joining, we've got a packed agenda, we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:18] Speaker 2: quick note, recording has started, captions on.
[00:25] Avery: first off big shout out to infra team, we pushed the Dedicated autoscaler into canary last week and, and latency has been much more stable, so thanks Samir and team.
[00:43] Samir (VP Eng): yeah, thanks. The autoscaler saw a 22 percent reduction in tail latency for multi-tenant workloads after we tuned the batching window and KV cache heuristics. There are still edge cases with very short sequences where batching actually hurts, so we added a new policy flag.
[01:05] Maya (CTO): to add, kernel selection improvements landed two weeks ago; for Llama-style models we now pick quantized kernels earlier in the pipeline which reduced p99 by about 9 to 12 ms on A100s in our internal tests. not perfect, but meaningful.
[01:28] Avery: awesome. Jon, take us through the numbers.
[01:32] Jon (CFO): sure. Quick headline: ARR run-rate is $42.3M, quarter-over-quarter growth 11 percent, gross margin improved by 3 points mainly from lower GPU spot costs and early Optimize wins. Burn runway extended to about 14 months at current pace. We still plan to be conservative on hires but will prioritize sales engineering and critical infra.
[02:00] Chris (Head of Sales): on the commercial side, we closed two mid-market deals for Dedicated this month and three pilots for Private deployments in regulated finance and health. Those pilots are our best path to ramp Dedicated commitments. Quick note: pricing feedback — customers want clearer unit economics for mixed-hosting (hosted + dedicated) so Leah will update the pricing page.
[02:33] Leah (Head of Product): yep, on that — product is reprioritizing a small set of roadmap items: we will move Private VPC peering and enhanced KMS integrations up by two sprints to support pilot timelines. That means one lower-priority UX improvement for the Console will slip to Q4. We'll share the updated deck later this week.
[03:00] Avery: can you clarify what the KMS change is, Leah?
[03:04] Leah: sure, we need to support customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS for on-prem and VPC deployments; right now our KMS path is fine for hosted but pilots require BYOK with rotation policies.
[03:20] Maya: adding to product — engineering has a rough patch for that but we scoped an API level change that should be minimally invasive. We'll need two security reviews before the pilot.
[03:35] Priya (Head of People): hiring update — we closed three IC offers and a senior infra manager; upcoming hires focus on SEs and CSMs to support Dedicated launch. Also re: comp, we'll publish the updated bonus plan for FY27 next week.
[03:55] Speaker 3: (audio glitch) sorry, lost Avery for a second.
[04:05] Avery: back — thanks. Okay questions from the crowd, we'll take a few pre-submitted and then live questions.
[04:12] Q (Slack): "Where are we with SOC2?"
[04:20] Jon: security — SOC2 Type II engagement starts next month, expected close by end of Q4. ISO work is queued and we'll try to run both in parallel. The security team will publish the control matrix and expected evidence timeline.
[04:45] Q: "Region availability for EU and APAC?"
[04:50] Chris: host availability — we're expanding dedicated capacity in eu-west and asia-south region via partners. Private deployments for APAC pilots are on-prem / partner-hosted for now. We'll post an availability map with expected dates.
[05:12] Q: "Any change to pricing?"
[05:17] Leah: no headline price change but we'll add clearer examples showing cost per request under mixed routing and batch strategies; Optimize will have guided recommendations to reduce unit cost.
[05:34] Speaker 4: some background noise, sorry.
[05:50] Maya: quick deep tech note — the KV cache pre-warming we introduced reduced cold-start token generation cost by about 18 percent for our bench set, but there are still pathological cases when customers stream huge context windows. We're building heuristics to evict stale prefixes and also testing a hybrid on-disk/memory approach.
[06:20] Samir: and on compilation we shipped a change to better choose matmul kernels for 8-bit quantized weights on newer GPUs; it's a modest perf win but consistent across models.
[06:38] Avery: great. Now product demo — Leah will show highlights from the new console telemetry.
[06:45] Leah: thanks. (screen share commentary) on the left you see per-route latency and cost heatmap, new token-level breakdowns, and a drift monitor that flags regression against control prompts. note, the drift monitor is early and we need more labeled prompts to reduce false positives.
[07:20] Speaker 1: (inaudible) can you repeat the drift definition?
[07:25] Leah: sure, drift here means change in distribution of outputs for a fixed prompt set causing drop in quality measured by our eval metrics. it's not perfect but it's useful as a canary.
[07:40] Q (live): "Will drift trigger auto-rollbacks?"
[07:45] Leah: not yet; the plan is alerts to SEs/owners with suggested rollback targets; automatic rollback is lower risk but we'll consider it later.
[08:00] Chris: sales POV — we'd like a one-page deck on drift for customers; helps explain why we do continuous evals. Leah will prep that.
[08:10] Avery: okay, switching to community & partnerships.
[08:14] Maya: partnering with two hardware vendors for memory-savings tech we discussed earlier. Pilot will run in October; if results hold we'll fold it into Dedicated offering as an optional profile.
[08:30] Q: "Are we competing with GenCloud here?"
[08:32] Chris: they came up in two RFPs; messaging is different — they push managed endpoints, we push a unified inference runtime across hosted/dedicated/private which resonates with platform teams. still, they are a competitor for mid-market deals.
[08:50] Audience question log: "how to get involved in pilots?"
[08:55] Avery: internal volunteers welcome, SEs will coordinate; if you want to help customer onboarding ping Chris and sign up in the sheet.
[09:05] (short pause)
[09:10] Jon: finance housekeeping — cost optimization efforts saved about $480k last quarter; one-off tax credit came through. We'll continue to track GPU spend by model family and region.
[09:26] Q: "Any layoffs or reorg?"
[09:29] Priya: no layoffs. small reorganizations to better align SEs with enterprise accounts; roles shifting but we'll share org charts.
[09:40] Live Q&A continues, people ask about repo access, eval processes, and the pilot criteria.
[10:02] Avery: quick recap — product to share updated deck, security to publish SOC2 timeline, SEs to run benchmarks with pilot customers, hiring continues with priority on SE and infra roles. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[10:18] End recording.
